specCitations.requirement: Campaign launch requires an authoritative canonical source (MODIFIED)
specCitations.text: Mission launch, Mech Bay readiness, fast-forward, campaign dashboard readiness, co-op launch, and materializer callers SHALL share the same admission guard. A consumer without an authoritative custom snapshot SHALL continue to block custom units rather than infer membership. Server materialization SHALL re-resolve selected saved construction before recording combat.

WHEN co-op receives a missing, foreign, stale, or revision-mismatched campaign snapshot THEN launch SHALL reject before composition or encounter launch AND the client SHALL NOT synthesize source identity, force membership, construction authority, or a stock fallback

testDesign.browser: The new describe routes the launch page's dynamic import of launchCoopMission through the REAL implementation (jest.requireActual, lazily, inside the delegating mock) with a spy ICampaignEncounterLauncherService substituted for the singleton. A denied launch therefore has to leave spy.created and spy.launched empty, which is the literal 'before composition or encounter launch' clause. The custom combat catalog refs and the co-op runtime roster projection are the two injected fixtures; the pre-existing suites keep the original light mock and were re-verified green.
testDesign.server: A force whose single assignment carries a custom-* unitId makes buildGameUnitsFromEncounter stamp unitRef='custom-coop-atlas' (src/services/encounter/encounterToGameSession.ts:199), which is what puts EncounterService.launchEncounter on the saved-construction branch. options.readCustom is the injected authority: null for the stale case, a snapshot minted for a different id for the foreign case, and an exact-id snapshot (parseCustomCombatDefinition over the Atlas AS7-D catalog JSON) for the admitted case.

findingsNotClosuresButWorthRecording: CORRECTED per review RE-1. The co-op launch page derives BOTH snapshot.{campaignId,matchId,revision} AND expected.{campaignId,matchId,revision} from the same in-page sources (campaign.id, matchId, and one readCampaignLaunchHead result), so the 'snapshot_foreign' and 'snapshot_stale' denials in admitCampaignLaunch are structurally unreachable from THAT call site. The original wording then claimed those branches were 'already covered at the unit level in launchCoopMission.test.ts and canonicalCatalogAdmission.test.ts'. That was FALSE for canonicalCatalogAdmission.test.ts: both of its admitCampaignLaunch call sites (:194 and :220) pass a snapshot whose campaignId equals expected.campaignId with no matchId and no revision, so neither branch is ever entered there. TRUE STATE at the time of commit 33d1975fd: snapshot_foreign and snapshot_stale had coverage in exactly ONE place, src/lib/campaign/coop/__tests__/launchCoopMission.test.ts:259-268, as two bare admitCampaignLaunch(...) helper calls whose booleans are folded into the CAMP-01D wave-artifact assertion bundle at :292-294 -- not named rows, not run through launchCoopMission, and a regression there reports as a wave-assertion failure rather than as a named scenario failure. The missing-snapshot branch (canonicalCatalogAdmission.ts:187-190) had NO coverage anywhere in src/. Commit 83c691741 closes all three with named rows; see reviewResponse below.

launchCoopMission's per-unit fallback for a deploying unit id absent from the admission's selectedUnits is `{ unitId, unitName: unitId }` with no unitRef, which admitCanonicalExactReference denies as 'unit_ref_unresolved'. That fallback is fail-closed, which is why the real-implementation delegation in the browser rows required seeding the co-op runtime roster rather than leaving it undefined.
nonClaims: ADJECTIVE COVERAGE OF COMMIT 33d1975fd: 0 of the 4 campaign-snapshot adjectives the spec scenario names ('missing, foreign, stale, or revision-mismatched campaign snapshot') are covered by that commit.
